content:
connes-rigidity is a personal experiment to digest the proofs of counterexamples found for Connes' rigidity conjecture: Chapter 4 of ten-proofs-oai by OpenAI, the independent and concurrent work arXiv:2608.02327 by Shuoxing Zhou, and the independent reproduction by Anthropic.

To me, the interesting bit on math is that the counterexamples arose from the information loss along the construction paths under control conditions, and the 3 works here followed different approaches. I then wondered whether the formalization process would surface some of the insights, and had ideas on how autonomously this could be done by agents while holding up to a standard suitable for human examination and digestion. For the slightly more elaborated motivation, see here in the companion formalization notes.

Currently, this project focused on formalizing the Zhou approach which is more accessible to me, also a setting with managable complexity. It is now complete relative to the cited EJZK input (the author had done the formalization to the same extent himself, so the Lean work here is just an independent reproduction at best, but I was surprised when it is done without major difficulties and within few days). I steered lightly during the process, GPT-5.6 Sol did most of the work per rubrics of Tau Ceti and some of my homebrew Lean skills. Most of the human effort were devoted into verification, audits, and the companion formalization notes where I documented the "Disclosure of AI use" near the end, but in a style that agents acknowledge human contributions.

Sharing here because the comparison and discussion of the 3 approaches along with the missing bits of Mathlib and Tau Ceti roadmaps (the current formalization is complete with sole dependency on Mathlib, but formalizing all of 3 proofs would need more), and how this project was done might be interesting to some, and some might also point out mistakes I made.

This work is not affiliated with or endorsed by any of the 3 parties. It is just an experiment out of curiosity. Suggestions and critics welcome.
Your comparator challenge file could be simplified. It has definitions that are already in mathlib.

Kim Morrison said:

Your comparator challenge file could be simplified. It has definitions that are already in mathlib.

Thanks for pointing that out, it seems that I can remove less than expected, and the changes would also affect the formalization side too.

Agent eval summary

Pinned-Mathlib overlap is narrower than it first appears. Connes.conjugacyClass is a genuine duplicate of Mathlib conjugatesOf and is the surgical refactor candidate. The apparent projection-order duplicate is not safely removable: Mathlib lacks the required C⋆/star-order instances for the concrete von Neumann subalgebra carrier, so the local multiplication-based adapter remains necessary. Property (T), the ℓ² reindexing, unitary regular representation, von Neumann generation, trace, and normal tracial-equivalence boundaries have no direct pinned-Mathlib replacement. Updating the four consumer proofs to Mathlib IsConj; the first full build exposed representation-shape mismatches that I am fixing without weakening IsICC.
I stopped reading after seeing the conjugacy class stuff. Happy to look again when it's fixed.

Kim Morrison said:

Happy to look again when it's fixed.

I bumped and probed mathlib a few times (now pinned at a recent commit on v4.34.0-rc2) to simplify the challenge file, and adapted the proof to the resulting API changes. There were 56 heartbeat overrides in the repo, I had also asked agents to reduce that to 4 real hotspots with a proper threshold.

Now we use Mathlib's conjugatesOf, removed local wrappers like ProjectionLE, GroupsIsomorphic in favor of Mathlib counterparts. A few separate refactor/golf runs on challenge file and the proof side, including one pass by Archon-Horizon, did result in a reduction of loc and more natural math layering to the best of my knowledge. Some overlapping APIs were then identified by additional reviews after refactor, and addressed. Metadata are updated to meet the basic requirements of Palomar submission. A final eyeballing pass led me to simplify vonNeumannClosure with Mathlib's VonNeumannAlgebra.commutant.

The proof-structure changes have been synced to the forest notes, I also asked the agent to write notes to break down the challenge file, and triage whether a definition is really the domain-specific foundation, conventional adaptation or potentially general and worth upstreaming to Mathlib.

The Challenge file is now 154 loc (reduced from 192 at 8b38a02 ) by tokei, and should be more manageable to check faithfulness to Zhou’s paper.
